correctness.rationale: The step-two constraint transformation exactly partitions cycle neighborhood inequalities into one odd chain (n odd) or two independent chains (n even). Summing pair constraints produces a tight minimum and a complete equality-case classification. Even chain length forces all constraints tight and alternating labels; odd chain length with odd k has exactly one unit-slack edge and precisely m choices; odd chain with even k has the unique constant solution. Multiplication and endpoint-versus-interior choices prove the support polynomial including n=4. Standalone original-neighborhood brute force 18 cases and independent DP 112 cases both returned VERIFY_OK; finite checks only corroborate the general proof.

value.rationale: Provides a natural complete optimizer-classification invariant for a recently active integer total domination model, substantially stronger than the known optimum weight. It distinguishes cycle lengths that admit sparse optimal coverage from lengths where every optimal solution must assign a strictly positive resource at all vertices, and gives exact support-size multiplicities for every n>=3 and all k>=2. The sharp 4-divisibility phase transition and all-solution counts matter when deployment flexibility and supported-vertex count differ despite equal total weight; no general theorem or conjecture resolution is claimed.
